artboards.title: Home — the job as ground, not a lane
A — Logging a verdict, in place
B — The year with the job on it

annotations.text:
THE TEST FOR WHETHER SOMETHING IS A LANE: could it go quiet for six weeks without you noticing?

If yes, it is a lane — the silence is the finding, and the rail is how you see it.
If no, it is not. The job cannot silently go quiet; you would be unemployed. Drawing fifty-two identical fat bars for it is decoration, not information.

And on overlap: one lane per block, and the choosing IS the reflective act. But that only survives contact with real life if the moment of hesitation is rare. A good lane set is one where roughly nine blocks in ten are obvious and the tenth makes you think for two seconds. If every block is ambiguous, the lanes are wrong — not the rule.

Four lanes here, down from six. MONEY is gone: Cadence already does it, and a lane that duplicates a tool you already use produces no surprise. THE JOB is gone as a lane — see the variant below. What remains are the four that can go quiet on you.

Four rails, 81px each. Fewer lanes means bigger marks, more air, and a year view you can actually read.

WHY 'THE WORK' HAD TO GO. It was the right idea with a name that swallows everything: the portfolio is the work, the steps are the work, the body is the work. Every lane except the job is 'the work' — it is the name of the app, not of a lane.

So name lanes by their OBJECT, not their spirit. CRAFT is being good at something. RECOVERY is meetings, the 12x12, the step writing, the call you made instead. Both are the summons; only one is about becoming good at a thing.

RECOVERY rather than SOBER, because SOBER names a state and the lane holds hours. If sobriety itself wants recording, it is the same shape as the job: a condition, not a stack of blocks. PROGRAM would work too, and is what you would actually say out loud.

All four names are placeholders. Change any of them in one line.

The job as ground rather than as a lane.

One verdict a day — did it enlarge or diminish you — with no size, because the size is always the same and you already know it. Blank on a day off, which is why the ribbon has gaps exactly at weekends without anything drawing them.

The volume of the job carries nothing. The valence carries a great deal: 'it took the same forty hours every week and stopped enlarging me in March' is a finding, and it is invisible in every other tool you own.

LOCKED. B FULL / FADED for the day mark, 1 STACKED for the week cell.

One rule holds at both resolutions: footprint means size, fill means enlarged, fade means diminished. Rejected options kept and dimmed — a decision without its reasons is just a preference.

A — HOW YOU LOG A VERDICT.

No screen and no prompt: the ribbon cell IS the control. Tap today's cell and three cells open in place under the row; tap one and it closes. Two taps, no navigation, and the day grid never leaves the screen.

This is deliberately not the 3x2 grid. There is no size to pick, so a full screen for one bit of information would read as a chore — which is exactly how a daily ask turns into a streak you resent.

NO WORK is the third cell rather than a default, because a day off is a real answer and the app should never guess it from the calendar.

Skip a day and the cell stays blank. Nothing counts it, nothing mentions it, and no badge appears.

B — DOES IT SURVIVE AT 11px A WEEK?

Two encodings of the same job, side by side, so the answer is visible rather than argued.

LEFT keeps the day grain: five 4px marks a week. It turns to dither. You can just about see the year darken, but no particular week says anything, and the texture competes with the lanes for attention.

RIGHT draws the week the way a lane is drawn — same length every time, only the solid/faded split moving. The March turn is unmissable, and it costs one encoding rule rather than two.

The blank rows are the one week off in August, drawn by nothing.

If the ribbon ships, it ships as the right-hand version at year scale and the day version on the home screen. Same fact, drawn at the resolution each view can carry.

C — WHERE THE CLUTTER STARTS. Sooner than expected, and not for the reason I expected.

The second ribbon is SOBER, and look at what it draws: twenty-one identical cells, an unbroken column. That is a streak. No number counts it, but the eye counts it, and the day it breaks the screen will say so louder than any counter — which is the one thing this app promised not to do.

It also does not fit the encoding. Solid means enlarged and faded means diminished everywhere else; here solid would mean 'yes' and faded would mean 'no', which is a different question wearing the same clothes.

And it is already covered: RECOVERY is the lane that holds meetings, the 12x12 and the step writing — the hours you actually gave. Note that the ribbon even collides with that lane's colour.

One condition is a design. Two is a dashboard with a streak in it.
